project_1_short_description: Full-stack whiteboard app embedding Excalidraw's React component inside Svelte with auth and persistent workspaces.
project_1_long_description: A full-stack whiteboard application built with SvelteKit, embedding Excalidraw's React component within a Svelte app to demonstrate cross-framework integration. Features user authentication (email/password + GitHub OAuth via Better Auth), persistent canvas storage with PostgreSQL and Drizzle ORM, folder organization, and transactional emails with Resend. React is initialized inside a Svelte 5 $effect() via the @attach directive, making it active only within that single component lifecycle while the rest of the app is pure Svelte.
project_1_highlight_1: Cross-framework integration: React component inside Svelte 5
project_1_highlight_2: User auth with email/password + GitHub OAuth via Better Auth
project_1_highlight_3: Persistent workspaces with PostgreSQL + Drizzle ORM
project_1_highlight_4: Transaction emails (verification, password reset) via Resend
project_1_highlight_5: Lazy-loaded React rendering isolated from Svelte runtime
project_2_short_description: Next.js anime and manga database powered by the AniList GraphQL API, styled with Tailwind CSS, with i18n and favorites.
project_2_long_description: An application built with Next.js that connects to the AniList API using GraphQL to display detailed information about anime and manga. Features include browsing by genre, popularity, and release dates, an integrated search bar, a favorites section persisted in Local Storage, and a global language switcher (English/Spanish) that stores user preference across sessions.
project_2_highlight_2: Client-side favorites persisted in Local Storage
project_2_highlight_3: Global language switcher (EN/ES) with persistent preference
project_2_highlight_4: Advanced search and filtering for anime and manga
project_3_short_description: Netflix clone built with Svelte and SvelteKit, developed as a learning project with custom implementation.
project_3_long_description: A Netflix clone built with Svelte and SvelteKit. Developed while following a Udemy course, but implemented with my own approach and design decisions. Covers component composition, routing, and responsive layouts in SvelteKit.
project_4_short_description: Curated collection of CSS, SVG, and GSAP animation techniques built with SvelteKit.
project_4_long_description: A visual gallery and learning resource demonstrating various web animation techniques including pure CSS transitions, keyframes, clip-paths, SVG path animations, and GSAP ScrollTrigger effects. Built with SvelteKit to organize multiple animation categories with a floating navigation menu.
project_4_highlight_1: Pure CSS transitions, keyframes, and clip-path effects
project_4_highlight_4: Floating navigation across multiple animation categories
project_5_short_description: My first React project -- a character database for browsing Blue Archive data.
project_5_long_description: One of my earliest projects and my first time building with React. A frontend app built with TypeScript and Vite that loads character data from a local JSON file. Simple but meaningful -- it's where I learned React component architecture and state management.
project_6_short_description: Vue.js notes app with register/login, CRUD notes, and admin mode, connected to a Hono backend.
project_6_long_description: Vue.js frontend for a notes application. Features user registration and login, full CRUD for notes with title and description, and an admin mode to view and delete other users. Connects to a separate Hono backend deployed on Cloudflare Workers.
project_6_highlight_3: CRUD notes with title and description
project_7_short_description: Hono REST API backend for the Vue notes app, deployed on Cloudflare Workers with Drizzle ORM.
project_7_long_description: Backend API built with Hono running on Cloudflare Workers. Provides REST endpoints for user authentication, note CRUD operations, and admin user management. Uses Drizzle ORM for database access and Bun as the local development runtime.
project_8_short_description: C# console application that scrapes and structures data from the Blue Archive Wiki.
project_8_long_description: A console application built with C# and .NET that crawls the Blue Archive Wiki to extract and structure character and game data. Uses HtmlAgilityPack with XPath to parse and extract HTML content, Entity Framework with SQLite for data persistence, and dependency injection for service management.
project_8_highlight_2: HtmlAgilityPack with XPath for HTML parsing
project_8_highlight_4: Entity Framework with SQLite for data persistence
project_8_highlight_5: Structured data output from unstructured wiki content
project_9_short_description: Vanilla JS image gallery searching anime images via the yande.re API. *(archived -- API no longer works client-side)*
project_9_long_description: A simple image gallery built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Searches for anime images using the yande.re public API. Features search by character name, anime name, and tags. Archived because the yande.re API now requires server-side access and no longer works from the browser.

project_10_long_description: Angular application that connected to the Marvel public API to display characters, comics, creators, series, and events. Featured search and category browsing. Archived because the Marvel public API was discontinued.

project_11_short_description: SvelteKit note-taking app with auth, workspaces, and page-based notes -- a course project I archived.
project_11_long_description: A note-taking application built with SvelteKit following a Udemy course, extended with full authentication (email/password + GitHub OAuth via Better Auth), workspace organization, and page-based notes. about_p1: I'm Gonzalo — Nyasper on GitHub. A self-taught web developer with four years of dedicated self-study. While I'm looking to take my first professional step in the industry, I have spent these years building solid projects, learning continuously, and refining my skills. No CS degree, no bootcamp — just relentless curiosity and more broken projects than I'd like to admit. That journey is what brought me here.
about_p2: Most of my experience is within the JavaScript ecosystem, although I enjoy exploring new technologies and tools whenever I can.
about_p3_before: If you're reading this — thank you. Truly. I hope something here catches your attention.
faq_q1_question: What keeps me hooked on coding?
faq_q1_answer: Programming feels like a game where every bug is a boss fight and every project unlocks a new skill tree. I started because I was curious, but I stayed because I enjoy the process of building things and figuring out how they work.
faq_q2_question: What do I enjoy most about programming?
faq_q2_answer: That moment when something finally clicks after hours of being completely lost. Your brain was working the whole time without telling you — and then, out of nowhere, it just hands you the answer. Also the fact that the ceiling doesn't exist. There's always a deeper layer, a better pattern, something you hadn't considered, no matter how much you learn, there's always another level waiting.
faq_q3_answer: "Nyasper" is the Japanese name of Espurr — a Pokémon. That psychic cat with an existential stare on my GitHub profile picture. Somehow the name just stuck with me.
faq_q4_question: Why so many frameworks? Are you an expert in all of them?
faq_q4_answer: Definitely not an expert in all of them — and that's kind of the point. I believe knowing a tool exists is half the battle. You don't need to master everything, but you need to know when to reach for it. A carpenter doesn't use the same tool for every job.
faq_q5_answer: Not because it's trendy. I use it because it gets out of my way. Less boilerplate, cleaner code, and it makes building feel closer to thinking. Once you write a component in Svelte, going back feels like typing with oven mitts.
faq_q6_question: What about .NET? Didn't you specialize in the JS ecosystem?
faq_q6_answer: JavaScript was my entry point, but C# and .NET is where I actually learned to think like a developer. OOP, design patterns, dependency injection — concepts that changed how I approach every problem, regardless of the language. It doesn't get the spotlight on this portfolio, but it has a permanent place in how I think.
faq_q7_answer: I think it's the most interesting and uncomfortable shift the industry has seen in a while. AI isn't replacing developers — it's redefining what one developer can do alone. I'd rather be someone who adapts than someone who complains, and honestly, I'm curious where this goes.
faq_q8_question: What's something programming taught me outside of coding?
faq_q8_answer: Probably patience. Debugging teaches you very quickly that being frustrated doesn't solve problems — understanding them does.
